sentences.text: Hon'ble Supreme Court held that in a money decree normally there shall be no stay till decretal amount is deposited or security is given for the said amount.
Only for adequate and cogent reasons stay may be granted.
(emphasis supplied)

7. Learned counsel further submits that in the present case, the claimants who are the poor and downtrodden dependents of the deceased have not received the compensation amount, therefore,
the interim order should be vacated and the execution case should proceed or otherwise the appellant may be directed to deposit the award amount in the Executing Court.
8.
Mr. Durgesh Kumar Singh, learned counsel for the appellant-Insurance Company has opposed the application.

It is his submission that on bare perusal of the judgment of the learned Tribunal, it would appear that there was no credible evidence on Patna High Court MA No.732 of 2018(7)
dt.20-01-2023 the record to accept that the deceased was working as a plumber technician and that his earning was Rs.350 per day.

It is submitted that the learned Tribunal has, though, recorded that no documentary evidence has been filed on behalf of the claimants regarding income of the deceased but the Tribunal has concluded that the daily income of the deceased is fixed at Rs.250/- for the purpose of calculation of quantum of compensation.

On this, future prospect has been allowed at the rate of 50% which is not in consonance with the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited versus Pranay Sethi & Others reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant, however, admits that the Tribunal has allowed lessor amount on account of loss of consortium, funeral expenses and loss of estate and as against the minimum amount of Rs.70,000/- which should have been allowed together on all these heads, the Tribunal has allowed only a sum of Rs.20,000/-.
Learned counsel for the Insurance Company submits that during the relevant time, the daily remuneration of a skilled worker was Rs.119/- only.

Even if the total loss of dependency on account of death of the deceased is calculated taking the remuneration of a skilled worker during the relevant time, as per his calculation the compensation would be a maximum sum of Rs.5,90,000/-.

Learned counsel, however, submits that as an Patna High Court MA No.732 of 2018(7) dt.20-01-2023 unskilled worker, the compensation would be only Rs.3,86,200/- and as a semi-skilled worker, it would have been Rs.4,86,756/-.
10.

Learned counsel for the Insurance Company submits that the appellant is ready to abide by such terms and conditions which may be imposed by this Court for the present for the purpose of staying the execution of further proceeding in the learned court below during pendency of the appeal.

11. Having heard learned counsel for the appellant and learned counsel for the respondents, this Court finds that in this case by the impugned award a sum of Rs.11,17,500/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of filing of the claim petition till the date of final payment has been allowed in favour of the claimants.
The Insurance Company has been granted liberty to recover the compensation amount from the owner of the vehicle.
It is true that the award has a force of decree and in view of the settled law normally a money decree is not stayed.

In this connection,
this Court would briefly refer Order XLI Rule 5 and Order XLI Rule 6 CPC as under:-
"5. Stay by Appellate Court.-

(1) An appeal shall not operate as a stay of proceedings under a decree or order appealed from except so far as the Appellate Court may order, nor shall execution of a decree be stayed by reason only of an appeal having been preferred from the decree; but the Appellate Court may for sufficient cause order stay of execution of such decree.
( 2 ) Stay by court which passed the decree :--

Patna High Court MA No.732 of 2018(7) dt.20-01-2023 Where an application is made for stay of execution of an appealable decree before the expiration of the time allowed for appealing therefrom, the court which passed the decree may on sufficient cause being shown order the execution to be stayed.

(3) No order for stay of execution shall be made under sub-rule (1) or sub-rule (2)
unless the court making it is satisfied-- (a) that substantial loss may result to the party applying for stay of execution unless the order is made;
(b) that the application has been made without unreasonable delay; and The Chairman, I C I C I Lombard General ... vs Rekha Devi on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/193712537/
3 (c) that security has been given by the applicant for the due performance of such decree or order as may ultimately be binding upon him.
(4) 2[Subject to the provision of sub-rule (3)], the court may make an ex parte order for stay of execution pending the hearing of the application.
[(5) Notwithstanding anything contained in the foregoing sub-rules, where the appellant fails to make the deposit or furnish the security specified in sub-rule (3) of rule 1, the court shall not make an order staying the execution of the decree.]
6. Security in case of order for execution of decree appealed from.

- (1) Where an order is made for the execution of a decree from which an appeal is pending, the Court which passed the decree shall,
on sufficient cause being shown by the appellant, require security to be taken for the restitution of any property which may be or has been taken in execution of the decree or for the payment of the value of such property and for the due performance of the decree or order of the Appellate Court, or the Appellate Court may for like cause direct the Court which passed the decree to take such security.
2. Subs. by Act 104 of 1976, s. 87, for certain words (w.e.f. 1-2-1977).
3. Ins. by Act 104 of 1976, s. 87 (w.e.f. 1-2-1977). Patna High Court MA No.732 of 2018(7)
dt.20-01-2023 (2) Where an order has been made for the sale of immovable property in execution of a decree,and an appeal is pending from such decree, the sale shall, on the application of the judgment-debtor to the Court which made the order, be stayed on such terms as to giving security or otherwise as the Court thinks fit until the appeal is disposed of."
12.
In the case of Atma Ram Properties (P) Ltd. (supra), the Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that normally money decree is not stayed.

In para '9', the Hon'ble Apex Court held as under:-
"9.....The power to grant stay is discretionary and flows from the jurisdiction conferred on an appellate court which is equitable in nature.
To secure an order of stay merely by preferring an appeal is not a statutory right conferred on the appellant.
So also, an appellate court is not ordained to grant an order of stay merely because an appeal has been preferred and an application for an order of stay has been made...."
13. In the present case, this Court finds that this appeal is of the year 2018 and the order of interim stay was passed as back as on 01.10.2019.

This Court agrees with the submission of learned counsel for the respondents that in view of the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Asian Resurfacing of Road Agency Private Limited (supra) the interim order has lost its efficacy.
